The thr-proximal counter-clockwise description D is presented as the exact mirror naming of the same ton-azi-thr interval under the opposite minute/landmark convention, thr → azi → ton counter-clockwise, and with the landmark nomenclature used in options A,B,C,E the conventionally quoted early-entry Hfr is the ton-proximal clockwise donor.

D camp – Colleagues 13,14,7 – insists on strict first-marker identity under the standard 100-min numbering. With origin near ton clockwise the entry order in that neighbourhood is origin~ton → tonB → azi → …, so tonB would be entered before azi and would be the marker with the longest expression window, not azi. The data require azi first. With the 24-28 min order a counter-clockwise origin placed on the thr side gives decreasing minute numbers

thr origin → azi/azis → tonB → …

so azi is the first bona fide selectable marker downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer, entered essentially as soon as transfer initiates and remaining the only donor product for a prolonged interval before tonB, pro, lac, str etc. appear. They argue the ton → azi → thr clockwise interval is the same DNA but the direct first-in description for azi-first entry is thr → azi → ton counter-clockwise, and that the mirror equivalence invoked by the A camp obscures the change in first-marker identity.

Options B Counterclockwise origin near lac, C Clockwise origin near pro and E Clockwise origin near str are repeatedly rejected because they place aziS many minutes downstream of the first encountered marker and cannot make aziS the leading prolonged marker.

Current public weight is numerically toward A Clockwise direction, origin near ton, with D Counterclockwise direction, origin near thr presented as the mirror description of the same ton-azi-thr neighbourhood under the opposite minute convention. Unresolved is which numbering convention/landmark naming the question expects: the ori-proximal clockwise ton naming used by the majority, or the 24-28 min thr-proximal counter-clockwise naming that makes azi strictly first downstream of the origin with no intervening tonB. The mirror equivalence is real geometrically; the apparent conflict is naming/numbering and whether tonB is treated as the immediate first marker versus aziS as the first selectable block. No new factual evidence has emerged in round 3 beyond reiteration of the polarity/naming dispute.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The mechanistic read-out is stable: prolonged first expression in an interrupted Hfr = the marker immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer, first entered, first scored, longest detectable.

Physical neighbourhood is unanimous: tonB-azi-thr cluster. The dispute is cartographic/polarity naming, not biology.

* Ori-proximal 75-90 min convention: … ton → azi → str → oriC → lac … clockwise. With this numbering azi lies immediately clockwise downstream of ton and immediately upstream of str/ori. * Classic 24-28 min convention: tonB ~25 min → azi ~26 min → thr ~27-28 min clockwise, i.e. thr → azi → tonB counter-clockwise. With this numbering an Hfr origin placed in the thr neighbourhood transferring counter-clockwise reads thr → azi → tonB… azi is first downstream.

A and D are mirror descriptions of the same ton-azi-thr interval.

Round 3 swing: Colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 now argue A. Clockwise direction, origin near ton, with the ori-proximal order ton → azi → str → ori → lac. 9.text:
Prolonged early scorable expression in an interrupted Hfr is the time-of-entry signature. The DNA that lies immediately downstream of the Hfr attachment site in the direction of transfer is the first donor DNA that can be made in the recipient and it therefore stays detectable the longest while more distal markers are still being pumped in. Prolonged early azis/azi therefore requires azis to be the first bona fide selectable marker downstream of the origin in the transfer polarity.

On the conventional K-12 circular linkage map used for the teaching set the azide block azis/azi is the ori-proximal member of the tonB/tonA – str/ori neighbourhood on the right arm. In the conventional clockwise minute description the local order is

… tonB/ton → aziS/azi → str → oriC → lac … clockwise

i.e. azi lies immediately clockwise downstream of the ton/ori-proximal region and immediately upstream of str/ori. In the 75-90 min ori-proximal numbering this is written … ton → azi → str → ori → lac … clockwise, the same physical ton–azi–thr interval that is often quoted in mirror form as thr → azi → ton counter-clockwise.

An Hfr whose F integration is in that ton/ori-proximal neighbourhood and which unwinds clockwise therefore reads out

origin ~ ton → ton first → aziS as the very next selectable segment → str → ori → lac → pro → thr …

AziS is entered essentially as soon as transfer initiates, is expressed as soon as it enters and is continuously supplied while the more distal clockwise markers lac, pro, thr, leu etc. are still being traversed. That gives the classic early entry, prolonged window of azis positivity before the later markers appear.

Origin near lac counter-clockwise, origin near pro clockwise and origin near str clockwise in the polarities quoted place aziS well downstream of the first marker that would be entered and cannot make aziS the leading, prolonged first-expressed marker.

The thr-proximal counter-clockwise description D, thr → azi → tonB counter-clockwise, is the exact mirror naming of the same ton-azi-thr physical interval under the opposite polarity/minute convention. With the landmark naming and clockwise minute convention used for options A, B, C and E the conventionally quoted first-in, longest-persistent Hfr for this cluster is the ton-proximal, ori-proximal clockwise donor.

That is

A. Clockwise direction, origin near ton

the classic ton-proximal clockwise Hfr that puts aziS at the very start of the incoming segment and accounts for the observed prolonged early azis expression before ton, str, lac, pro, thr etc. appear.

tonB ~25 min → azi/azis ~26 min → thr ~27-28 min clockwise

i.e. azi is immediately clockwise of tonB and immediately counter-clockwise of thr. That is the placement 7, 13 and 14 are citing and it is the neighbourhood used in the early mapping literature.

origin ~ ton → tonB → azi → thr …

The prolonged-azi window is a time-of-entry signature and the point that has not been resolved is what is actually first in the entry order on the map you use for the options.

On the classic 100-min K-12 map that underlies the historic Hfr P0 set the ton-azi-thr interval is the 24-28 min sector

tonB ~25 min → azi/azis ~26 min → thr ~27-28 min clockwise

i.e. azi is immediately clockwise of tonB and immediately counter-clockwise of thr. That is the placement 7, 13 and 14 are citing and it is the neighbourhood used in the early mapping literature.

Prolonged early azis therefore requires azis to be the very first bona fide selectable marker downstream of the origin in the transfer polarity, not the second.

With that order a clockwise origin placed on the ton side gives in that polarity

origin ~ ton → tonB → azi → thr …

TonB is then the first DNA in that neighbourhood to be injected and azi is second. Even treating tonB as a weak marker, the first selectable block downstream of a clockwise ton origin is tonB → azi, so tonB would carry the longest detectable window, with azi second. That is the opposite of the observed phenotype where azis is the prolonged early marker and is seen before ton and before the more distal markers.

A counter-clockwise origin placed on the thr side of the cluster gives the decreasing minute order

thr origin → azi/azis → tonB → …

Azi is now the first bona fide selectable marker downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer. It is made essentially as soon as transfer initiates and is continuously supplied while the chromosome is unwound counter-clockwise away from thr toward oriC. That is exactly the prolonged early azis window before tonB, pro, lac, str etc. are reached.

The mirror equivalence discussion is real geometrically: ton → azi → thr clockwise is the same physical DNA as thr → azi → ton counter-clockwise. The difference is labelling and first-marker identity. Option A as written is origin near ton clockwise. With the 24-28 min convention that puts tonB immediately downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer and azi second. The minute-number chaos visible in the A camp – ton quoted simultaneously as ~81-82 min, ~42 min and ~25 min with azi adjacencies shifting accordingly – is a symptom of that polarity problem.

With the landmark names and the 24-28 min convention used to name the options, the description that puts azi immediately downstream of the origin with no intervening selectable marker is the thr-proximal counter-clockwise Hfr, thr → azi → tonB counter-clockwise. That is Counterclockwise direction, origin near thr.

I’ve been trying to reconcile the time-of-entry logic with the actual minute order you’re all using for the options, and I’m still stuck on first vs second marker identity.

Prolonged early scorable expression in an interrupted Hfr is a first-in signature: the marker that is immediately downstream of the attachment site in the direction of transfer is the first selectable DNA that can be made and it stays scorable the longest before more distal markers arrive. That means azi has to be the very first bona fide selectable marker downstream of the origin in the transfer polarity, not the second.

On the 100-min K-12 map that underlies the historic Hfr P0 mapping the ton-azi-thr interval is the 24-28 min sector that is consistently quoted as

tonB ~25 min → azi/azis ~26 min → thr ~27-28 min clockwise

i.e. azi is immediately clockwise of tonB and immediately counter-clockwise of thr. That is the order 7, 13 and 14 are quoting, and it is the order used in the classic mapping literature.

With that order a clockwise origin placed on the ton side gives the entry order in that polarity

origin ~ ton → tonB → azi → thr …

TonB is then the first DNA to be injected in that neighbourhood and azi is second. Even if tonB is treated as the integration landmark, the first selectable block downstream of a clockwise ton origin is tonB → azi, so tonB would be the marker with the longest detectable window, with azi second. That is in direct conflict with the observed phenotype where azis is the prolonged early marker and is seen before ton.

A counter-clockwise origin placed on the thr side of the same physical interval removes the intervening marker:

thr origin → azi/azis → tonB → … decreasing minutes

Azi is now the first bona fide selectable marker downstream of the origin in the direction of transfer. It is made as soon as transfer initiates and is continuously supplied while the donor unwinds counter-clockwise away from thr toward oriC. That is exactly the prolonged early azis window before tonB, pro, lac, str etc. are reached.

The ton-clockwise / thr-counter-clockwise mirror discussion is real geometrically, but it does not preserve first-marker identity. ton → azi → thr clockwise is the same DNA as thr → azi → ton counter-clockwise, but the marker that is first in one polarity is not first in the opposite polarity.

I also note the naming drift in the A discussion. The A bloc is now simultaneously citing ton ~25 min, ton ~42 min, ton ~75-85 min and azi ~26 min vs ~77-79 min, and it is itself invoking the str/ori-proximal label for what it calls a ton origin. Options A and E are worded as distinct landmarks, origin near ton clockwise vs origin near str clockwise, and the conventional teaching label for this ori-proximal Hfr is the str/ori-proximal Hfr. That confusion is why I think we need to be explicit about which minute convention and which landmark we are using for the options.

With the 24-28 min landmark names used in the options, the orientation that puts azi immediately downstream of the origin with no intervening selectable marker is the counter-clockwise direction with origin near thr, thr → azi → tonB counter-clockwise. That is the classic first-in, longest-persistent description for the prolonged early azis phenotype on the map the options are using.
